text:
eli: Heads-up — noticed steady memory growth on kv-cache hosts when sessions exceed ~8k tokens. trend looks like tiny free holes piling up during long contexts.
maya: can you paste the profiler output? is this allocator churn or KV backfill? :thinking_face:
eli: quick dump below, sampled from a repro run (12k token sessions, high-turn chat).
```
KV-backfill-sample:
  total_ops: 1_050_342
  allocations:
    tiny_slot (32B): 41.7%
    small_slot (128B): 27.4%
    mid_slot (1KB): 18.1%
    backfill_overhead: 12.8%
  mem_peak_before_compact: 11.9GB
  mem_post_compact: 7.6GB
  compaction_wall_time: 420ms (single-threaded)
  observed_tail: p99 mem-alloc spike during compaction window
```

samir: OK that `backfill_overhead` number is worrying. sounds like our reuse policy aggressively backfills partial slots but doesn't coalesce later. how are frees flagged?
carla: frees are deferred to epoch GC to avoid locking. that reduces lock contention but creates temporally scattered free fragments.
eli: exactly — we end up with lot of ~64-256B holes scattered across pages, allocator picks small-fit and creates internal fragmentation. over long sessions this accumulates and GC compaction only runs rarely -> mem growth.
maya: did you try bumping base block size to reduce fragmentation? e.g. 512B -> 2KB?
eli: did a quick A/B on a 10-node pool. change: `base_slot_size=2048` vs default `512`. results:
```
A: base=512 -> steady mem 11.6GB, p99 tail allocs high
B: base=2048 -> steady mem 8.1GB, p50 latency +1.8ms, p99 latency unchanged
```
notes: bigger base reduced number of free fragments but increased per-request padding; net memory wins in our long-context workloads.

samir: that's interesting — lower fragmentation but slight p50 hit. do we have per-model token/per-request distributions? maybe only some models benefit.
carla: added per-model histograms to the profiler yesterday. for long-chat models (seq>6k tokens) median slot reuse is 62% and reuse churn is low -> larger base helps. for short-turn workloads base=512 is better.
maya: could we do adaptive base sizing per routing policy? e.g., route long-contexts to hosts configured with base=2048, others keep 512.
eli: yeah smart routing could help. another idea: opportunistic backfill compaction during idle windows. instead of full GC, run a streaming coalesce that scans hot pages and merges adjacent frees. lower latency cost if we throttle it.
samir: agree — also consider tracking "sparsity score" per page: (#free_slots / total_slots) * variance(slot_sizes). if score > threshold, mark for background compaction.
carla: implementation note: background compaction needs to avoid touching live KV pointers. we'd need safe copy or stop-the-world for small affected page region. cost ~= copy_bytes / memcpy_throughput.
eli: I ran a microbenchmark for streaming coalesce algorithm (single-threaded) — results:
```
stream-coalesce (throttle=0.5):
  scan_rate: 120MB/s
  avg_pause_per_op: 0.6ms
  mem_reclaimed_per_min: ~430MB
  p99 latency impact during run: +12ms spikes (rare)
```

maya: those p99 spikes worry me on high-SLA customers. maybe restrict to low-priority nodes or run when queue_len < 5.
samir: or schedule compaction as canary: enable on 5% nodes for a day, compare mem & latency. if safe, rollout more. also add a circuit-breaker: abort compaction if outgoing qps > threshold.
eli: perf-bot emitted a regression alert yesterday tied to a compaction trial (link: https://perf.internal/alert/9832). it flagged p99 latency increased by 18ms on affected hosts during run.
perf-bot: perf-bot: Regression detected: kv-compaction-run increased p99 latency by +18ms on pool-22 at 2026-03-16T03:12Z. See dashboard -> https://perf.internal/d/kv/compaction-runs

carla: ok let's propose a hybrid plan:
- short-term: enable larger base_slot_size on long-context host pools (config flag). A/B with 10% traffic.
- mid-term: implement sparsity-score + streaming coalesce (throttled) with circuit-breaker.
- long-term: explore allocator redesign to export free ranges (+ coalescing on free) so we minimize epoch deferred frees creating scatter.

maya: schedule action items?
eli: I'll open a tiny RFC with benchmarks, config knobs, and rollout plan. will include microbench numbers above.
samir: I'll add routing changes to route long-context sessions to the tuned pools.
carla: I'll prototype the sparsity-score collector in the profiler agent.
maya: Thanks. let's sync Fri 11 for quick triage. :thumbsup:
